current_date: July 2014, amended April 2015 (document text: 'Adopted July 2014'; 'Amended under new legislation April 2015')
current_evidence: The council's Application forms page lists only this PDF ('Validation requirements') under Supporting documents and mentions no newer list or consultation. Two web searches found no later Dover local list.

issues.detail: The list is still the council's only published one, but it is 11+ years old and badly out of date. It cites the Core Strategy, the Land Allocations Local Plan, the Code for Sustainable Homes (withdrawn in 2015), NPPF 2012 paragraphs 24-27 and DMPO 1995. It does not cover statutory Biodiversity Net Gain, nutrient neutrality or Thanet Coast SAMM mitigation, and it predates Dover's new Local Plan (adopted 2024). The workbook flags it as Outdated, but users should be warned that the council's actual validation practice will differ, and a list more than 2 years old carries little weight under DMPO art. 11.
issues.evidence: Document text: 'Adopted July 2014'; Note 29 'Code for Sustainable Homes/BREEAM Pre-Assessment Statements'; no mention of BNG

issues.detail: The List date (2014-07-01) ignores the stated April 2015 amendment.

Several of the 34 numbered Notes have no app_type row. They are: Note 20 Landscape Character Assessment ('Development that would result in harm to the character of the landscape'); Note 23 Open Space Assessment ('All development on open spaces'); Note 29 Code for Sustainable Homes/BREEAM Pre-Assessment ('All applications (full and outline) of 1 (new build) dwelling or more' and non-residential new build of 100 sqm or more); and Note 30 Telecommunications Statement ('Any planning application for mast and antenna development by a mobile phone network operator'). Note 13 Biodiversity Survey and Assessment appears only under 'Change of use - prior approval', not under Full or Outline.
issues.evidence: Numbered Notes 20, 23, 29 and 30 in the main requirements table

issues.detail: Listed building consent shows only Photographs. It omits the Heritage Statement (Note 18: required for all listed building applications) and the Design and Access Statement (Note 8: 'All applications for Listed Building Consent will require a D&A Statement'). Householder shows only the Block plan, although these requirements are not limited to non-householder schemes: Heritage Statement ('All applications which have an impact on a heritage asset'), Tree Survey (trees or hedgerows on or next to the site), Parking and Access ('All applications that would result in a loss or increase in parking provision') and FRA (Flood Zones 2/3 where new bedroom space is created).
issues.evidence: Note 8: 'All applications for Listed Building Consent will require a D&A Statement'

issues.detail: Some trigger excerpts come from the wrong requirement. The CIL Additional Information row quotes the Note 26 Planning Statement text. The Ventilation/Extraction row quotes the Acoustic Report text. The Noise Impact Assessment row quotes only the acoustician-qualification sentence, not the trigger ('Proposals likely to generate noise in excess of current background levels'). The Planning Statement row gives content guidance instead of the trigger 'All development (excluding householder)'. The Affordable Housing row ('Any application must provide an Affordable Housing Statement...') overstates the trigger, which is 'All applications that generate the need for Affordable Housing'.
issues.evidence: Note 26 trigger: 'All development (excluding householder)'; Note 11: 'All applications that generate the need for Affordable Housing'

issues.detail: Many triggers are garbled table text or fragments. Examples: Environmental Statement ('4 of EIA: Guide to EIA Regulations 2 and 3...'); site levels/sections ('in Section ground levels Drawings On sloping sites...'), where the source says 'Where a proposal involves a change in ground levels'; Tree Survey (mixed column headers); Transport Assessment ('on Highways Transport Assessment NPPG published by Department for Transport.'); Parking ('development affecting parking provision.'); Sunlight ('gardens or amenity space.'); Archaeological ('include an archaeological desk top assessment and a field evaluation report.'); Drainage/SuDS ('Drainage details that will achieve Building Regulations Approval'), which is not the Note 17 trigger (sites over 1ha or with known drainage/flooding problems; 50+ dwellings or 1,000 sqm commercial for utilities).
issues.evidence: Note 6: 'Where a proposal involves a change in ground levels'; Note 17: 'Sites larger than 1 hectare; sites where there is known drainage or localised flooding problem'

issues.detail: The Ecological Survey is placed under 'Change of use - prior approval' because its text mentions 'change of use'. The source never mentions prior approval; the requirement covers planning applications that change, modify or demolish certain buildings. Photographs are placed under Listed building consent, but the requirement covers major development, conservation areas, AONB and parking changes as well. About 28 other rows are 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning'. Examples are Air Quality, FRA, Heritage, Tree Survey and Lighting. The source has no application-type matrix, and several of these also apply to outline and householder applications. Code for Sustainable Homes/BREEAM is expressly 'full and outline'.
issues.evidence: Biodiversity: 'Applications that involve the change of use/modification/demolition (including in part) of the following buildings must provide a protected species survey'

issues.detail: 'Parking provision / Parking plan', 'Highways / access details (visibility splays)' and 'Cycle parking details' all come from the single Note 24 Parking and Access Arrangements requirement. The Highways row's excerpt says nothing about visibility splays.
issues.evidence: Note 24: 'All applications will be required to provide details of existing and proposed parking provision, including cycle parking'

issues.detail: Some items are process text or advice, not requirements. Examples are 'Pre-application advice / engagement details' ('In all but the most straightforward cases ... more efficient if applicants have sought advice'), the 'Validation Disputes' paragraph (which also cites the obsolete DMPO 1995) and 'Annotated photographs and plans can be used to help describe ... a conservation area'. The Design and Access Statement row's excerpt ('This could be a stand alone report...') is guidance about another document, not a DAS trigger.
issues.evidence: Tab item: 'Validation Disputes This information has been prepared having regard to ...'

summary: Grokbot links Dover's only published list (July 2014, amended April 2015), which is current in the sense that nothing replaces it but is badly outdated (no BNG, pre-2024 Local Plan). Grokbot's extraction misses several Notes (Landscape Character, Open Space, CSH/BREEAM, Telecoms), swaps triggers between requirements and puts Ecology under prior approval.
